recent_posts.title: Fedora Asahi Remix 44 is now available
recent_posts.summary: Fedora Asahi Remix 44 is now available, bringing Fedora Linux 44 to Apple Silicon Macs. Key changes include retirement of vendored Mesa and virglrenderer packages in favor of upstream Fedora repositories, KDE Plasma 6.6 as the flagship desktop with a new Plasma Setup wizard replacing Calamares, and Plasma Login Manager replacing SDDM for new installs. A GNOME 50 variant, Fedora Server variant, and Minimal image are also available. Existing Fedora Asahi Remix 42/43 users can upgrade via KDE Plasma Discover or DNF System Upgrade; GNOME Software upgrades are not supported.

recent_posts.title: What’s New in Fedora KDE Plasma Desktop 44
recent_posts.summary: Fedora KDE Plasma Desktop Edition 44 has been released, shipping with KDE Plasma 6.6.4. Key new features include custom global theme creation, Wi-Fi QR code scanning, per-application volume control, a new grayscale colorblindness filter, a screen magnifier, OCR scanning in Spectacle, and new accessibility settings. Fedora-specific additions include a new Plasma Setup and Plasma Login Manager for fresh installs, and a new Plasma Keyboard on-screen input. General Fedora 44 changes include DNF 5 as the PackageKit backend and Qualcomm laptop support. Star Labs now offers preinstalled Fedora KDE as an option on their devices through the Fedora Ready program.

recent_posts.title: Sealed Fedora Atomic Desktop bootable container images
recent_posts.summary: Fedora Atomic Desktop now has sealed bootable container images available for testing. These images provide a fully verified boot chain from firmware to OS, combining systemd-boot, Unified Kernel Images (UKI), and composefs with fs-verity. Both systemd-boot and UKI are signed for Secure Boot (UEFI on x86_64 and aarch64), though test images use unofficial keys. The primary benefit is enabling passwordless disk unlocking via TPM in a secure-by-default manner. These are test-only images — not for production use — with root passwordless access and sshd enabled for debugging.

recent_posts.title: What’s New for Fedora Atomic Desktops in Fedora Linux 44
recent_posts.summary: Fedora Linux 44 brings several updates to its Atomic Desktop variants (Silverblue, Kinoite, Sway Atomic, Budgie Atomic, and COSMIC Atomic). Key changes across all variants include a moved issue tracker to the new Fedora forge, unified documentation, removal of FUSE version 2 libraries (affecting some AppImages and Plasma Vault backends), and dropping legacy pkla Polkit rules. Silverblue ships with GNOME 50, Kinoite includes KDE Plasma 6.6 with a new Plasma Login Manager replacing SDDM and an OEM-style first-boot setup. Budgie Atomic gains Wayland support with Budgie 10.10.2, and COSMIC Atomic reaches stable with version 1.0.8. Looking ahead, sealed bootable container images are ready for testing and a roadmap toward full Bootable Container support is underway.

recent_posts.title: How to Rebase to Fedora Linux 44 on Silverblue
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide for upgrading Fedora Silverblue to Fedora Linux 44 using either GNOME Software or the terminal. Covers pre-upgrade steps, the rebase commands via rpm-ostree, how to pin deployments, rollback procedures via GRUB or the rpm-ostree rollback command, and an FAQ addressing version skipping and rpm-fusion compatibility issues.

recent_posts.title: What’s New in Fedora Workstation 44
recent_posts.summary: Fedora Workstation 44 has been released, shipping with GNOME 50 as its default desktop environment. Key highlights include a range of GNOME 50 refinements covering accessibility, color management, and remote desktop. A new Digital Wellbeing feature introduces native Parental Controls for setting screen time limits and bedtimes directly from Settings. Default applications like the Document Viewer, File Manager, and Calendar have also received improvements. Users can upgrade via the official website, GNOME Software, or the terminal using dnf system-upgrade.

recent_posts.title: The Fedora Linux 44 Release is Here!
recent_posts.summary: Fedora Linux 44 is now available. Key highlights include GNOME 50 on Workstation, KDE Plasma 6.6 with a new login manager and setup wizard, Wine NTSYNC kernel module support for improved Windows app and game compatibility, MariaDB 11.8 as the new default version, OpenSSL certificate loading improvements, and Btrfs subvolume replacing the /boot partition in Fedora Cloud images. Existing users can upgrade easily, and fresh install media is available for all editions including Workstation, KDE, Atomic Desktops, and various spins.

recent_posts.title: Fedora Linux 44 virtual release party on April 24 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Fedora Linux 44 Virtual Release Party is scheduled for April 24, 2026, as a free half-day online event open to all. The schedule includes sessions on new features such as Nix package tool integration, DNF5 and PackageKit with KDE, Fedora Atomic Desktops updates (Silverblue, Kinoite, COSMIC), Packit as Fedora dist-git CI, a Server Working Group home server spin, Fedora Docs updates, and a preview of the upcoming Flock conference. Registration via Matrix/Element is required to attend.

recent_posts.title: GDB source-tracking breakpoints
recent_posts.summary: GDB is introducing an experimental feature called source-tracking breakpoints that automatically adjusts breakpoint line numbers when source code is edited and recompiled. When enabled with 'set breakpoint source-tracking enabled on', GDB captures a small window of surrounding source code at each breakpoint. On reload, it searches within a 12-line window to find the new location and updates the breakpoint accordingly. Limitations include requiring exact string matches (whitespace changes break it), a maximum 12-line search window, no support for pending breakpoints, ranged breakpoints, or inline functions expanding to multiple locations. The feature is not yet in a stable release but can be tested via a Fedora COPR repository or by building from source with the upstream patch applied.

recent_posts.title: Nominate Your Fedora Heroes: Mentor and Contributor Recognition 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Fedora Project is calling for nominations for its Contributor Recognition 2026 program, celebrating exceptional mentors and contributors who have shaped the Fedora community. Nominations are open until May 15, 2026, with winners to be announced at Flock To Fedora 2026 in coordination with the Fedora Mentor Summit. Community members are encouraged to submit nominations via a provided Google Form.
